steps.name: QC and shallow-sample triage (sample_01)
caveats: sample_01's ~4x lower depth produces a small size factor; do not exclude it on depth alone — a shallow sample that still clusters with its group is normally retained, so the PCA check decides.
With only 12 samples PCA is indicative, not a formal outlier test; present it as such.
If counts are non-integer, note it and carry the treatment decision (treat as counts) forward to the DE step rather than silently rounding.
steps.context: Files: /eval-four-models-v2-without-mouse-two-group-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon gene-level, row names are mouse gene symbols) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-mouse-two-group-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows x 2 columns: sample, condition; HFD vs chow, 6 per group, unpaired, single batch). The data profile explicitly flags sample_01's library size as ~4x below the median and does not record whether Salmon applied effective-length correction. No network access: the two files above are the only inputs.
steps.question: Of the 12 mouse liver libraries, what is the QC state, and specifically how far does sample_01 — library size ~4x below the median — deviate from its own condition group, and do the Salmon counts look like raw integers or length-corrected decimals?
constraints: Load the count matrix and the sample table, and verify sample IDs match 1:1 between the two files before any computation.
Check whether count values are integers (raw counts) or non-integer (effective-length-corrected) and record the result explicitly — the profile does not say which was delivered.
Compute per-sample library sizes and DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors; report sample_01's size factor relative to the median.

PCA on log2-CPM (or DESeq2 VST) colored by condition; compute sample_01's distance to its condition-group centroid and to the overall mean in PC space, and state whether sample_01 separates from its group.
The primary analysis retains all 12 samples (6v6). sample_01 is handled as a sensitivity exclusion in the DE step, not removed here — do not drop it unilaterally.
No downloads; all inputs are the two provided files.
steps.description: Per-sample QC and an explicit triage of the shallow sample_01, producing a documented retain/exclude decision that drives the DE design.
acceptance_criteria: QC table (per sample: condition, library size, size factor) and a PC1-PC2 plot colored by condition saved as artifacts.
Explicit written verdict: integer vs non-integer counts, sample_01's depth ratio and PC-space distance, and the retained primary design (all 12 samples plus a sensitivity run).

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: HFD vs chow, with and without sample_01
caveats: Small n per group: expect large but unstable log2FCs on low-count genes; apeglm shrinkage is required for ranking, not optional.
Do not add batch or other covariates — the design is single-batch and unpaired.
sample_01's shallow depth inflates variance for the genes it contributes to; the sensitivity run exists to bound that effect, so both results must be reported even if the primary looks fine.
steps.context: Primary object: the Salmon gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples) with the condition design from metadata.csv. T1S1 supplies the QC verdict (size factors, PCA) and the integer-vs-decimal determination on the counts. Single batch, unpaired — no batch term exists to add. n=6 per group is low power; interpret accordingly.
steps.question: Which genes change expression between HFD and chow mouse liver (6v6, unpaired), and how robust is the differentially expressed gene set to excluding the shallow sample_01?
constraints: Model: DESeq2, design ~ condition, contrast HFD vs chow with HFD as the numerator of log2FC.
Shrink log2FC with apeglm (lfcShrink, type='apeglm') before any ranking or reporting.

Run the primary analysis on all 12 samples, plus a sensitivity analysis with sample_01 excluded (per the T1S1 verdict); report the overlap of the DE gene sets at padj < 0.05 and the maximum/median shift in shrunk log2FC among shared genes.
Significance: padj < 0.05 (FDR) as the primary cutoff; also tabulate padj < 0.1. Do not present raw-p-only genes as findings.
Outputs: full ranked table (gene symbol, baseMean, shrunk log2FC, padj, per-group mean counts) for both runs; volcano plot; heatmap of the top 50 genes (padj < 0.05 by |shrunk log2FC|).
If T1S1 found the counts to be non-integer (length-corrected), record that DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization was applied anyway and flag it as a caveat in the results.
State the power caveat in the write-up: with 6 samples per group, FDR-controlled p-values at n=12 have optimistic reliability, and individual-gene claims beyond the ranked table are hypotheses.
steps.description: Ranked differentially expressed gene list for HFD vs chow mouse liver with apeglm-shrunk LFCs, plus a leave-out sensitivity comparison for the shallow sample_01.
acceptance_criteria: DE table with gene, baseMean, shrunk log2FC, and padj for both the primary (12-sample) and sensitivity (11-sample) runs, plus a written comparison of the two runs.
Volcano plot and top-gene heatmap saved as artifacts.
The shallow-sample sensitivity result is reported, not just the primary run.

steps.name: Hallmark pathway enrichment (MSigDB mouse hallmark) on the DE ranked list
caveats: At n=6 per group the significant-gene lists can be small, which weakens ORA; the full-list fgsea is the primary test and ORA is the complement — say so if ORA lists are sparse.
fgsea assumes the ranking is informative across the full list; do not re-rank only the significant genes.
Salmon gene-level rows should be plain symbols; if any row carries a non-symbol suffix, resolve it, count what was dropped, and report the count.
steps.context: Input: the ranked gene list from T1S2 (primary all-12 run; include the sensitivity run if it materially differs). Gene IDs are mouse symbols (Salmon gene names, MGI-style). The environment provisions the MSigDB mouse hallmark gene sets (2026.1 release, species-matched MGI symbols) as the pathway reference — use these; the human hallmark, human GO, human oncogenic, and rat sets are wrong-species for this data and must not be used.
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways are enriched among the up- and down-regulated HFD genes in mouse liver?
constraints: Use only the mouse hallmark gene set collection; do not apply human or rat sets to mouse symbols.

Before running, verify symbol matching: count how many of the 12,000 matrix genes (and how many DE genes) are absent from the hallmark universe and report the unmatched fraction; if the DE-list match rate is below ~80%, stop and report the mismatch rather than run on a silently truncated list.

Run fgsea on the full 12,000-gene list ranked by signed -log10(p) (padj, using p where padj is undefined); report set name, NES, and padj with a significance threshold of padj < 0.05, and record the direction (up/down).

Complement with over-representation analysis of the up- and down-regulated gene lists (padj < 0.05; if either list has fewer than ~10 genes, use the top 50 by |shrunk log2FC| within that direction) with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
Report the top 10 up- and top 10 down-enriched hallmark pathways with their leading-edge genes.
If the T1S2 sensitivity run (sample_01 excluded) yields a materially different significant-pathway set, state both and which is primary.
steps.description: Hallmark pathway enrichment of the HFD vs chow ranked gene list using the species-matched MSigDB mouse hallmark sets, with fgsea as the primary test and ORA as complement.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway table (set name, NES or enrichment score, padj, direction, leading-edge genes) for both fgsea and the ORA complement.
Dot or ridge plot of the top hallmark pathways saved as an artifact.
Explicit statement of the gene-set collection used (MSigDB mouse hallmark, 2026.1) and the symbol match rate.

plan.title: HFD vs chow mouse liver: DE genes + hallmark enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: Unpaired bulk RNA-seq of mouse liver: 6 high-fat diet (HFD) vs 6 chow, single batch, 12,000-gene Salmon gene-level count matrix. The data profile flags sample_01 at ~4x below median library size and does not record whether Salmon length correction was applied, so QC comes first: quantify sample_01's impact (size factors, PCA distance, integer-vs-decimal check) and keep the primary design at all 12 samples (6v6), with the shallow sample handled as a sensitivity exclusion in the DE step rather than dropped unilaterally. DE is DESeq2 (design ~ condition, single batch, apeglm-shrunk LFCs, FDR-controlled) run twice — primary 12-sample and 11-sample sensitivity — so the shallow sample's effect on the gene list is bounded rather than assumed. Pathway enrichment then answers the 'which hallmark pathways' half of the question using the environment's species-matched MSigDB mouse hallmark gene sets (MGI symbols, 2026.1) — not the human or rat collections — on the full ranked list (fgsea) with an over-representation complement for the significant genes. Order matters: the QC verdict drives the DE design, and the DE ranked list drives the enrichment.
